source.title: Symmetry Induces Structure and Constraint of Learning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports test accuracy after a symmetry-based parameterization, but does not measure the training–test gap or test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The ResNet18 experiment reports test accuracy for a symmetry-based parameterization and vanilla model. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, generalization measures, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study tests how parameter symmetries induce sparsity, low rank and neuron homogeneity. None of its results tests V1–V8. Its CIFAR-10 accuracy comparison evaluates its own symmetry-based parameterization without any of the interventions or comparisons those versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the central conclusion: mirror symmetries induce structural constraints favored by sufficiently strong weight decay or gradient noise. The authors describe both reduced expressivity and potential generalization benefits from ignoring noisy features. The ResNet18 comparison establishes similar test accuracy, rather than a substantial generalization improvement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a symmetry-based parameterization in a ResNet18 experiment; it does not reproduce the listed original studies' generalization-gap tests.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight decay varies in the ResNet18 activation-correlation experiment, but the reported comparison concerns activation structure rather than the listed generalization claims.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla and DCS ResNet18 both reach approximately 93% CIFAR-10 test accuracy, with DCS slightly higher.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding per-parameter rescaling symmetry preserves approximately the same held-out accuracy in this ResNet18 training setup.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The reported ResNet18 comparison gives test accuracy but not training accuracy or a direct generalization-gap measure; numerical uncertainty is not stated.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance-level held-out performance on random labels.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of learned local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The decisive issue is the absence of comparisons matching V1–V8, rather than the absence of training accuracy alone. The Hessian analysis does not test V7, and the discussion of batch size concerns attraction to constrained solutions rather than V5's held-out-performance penalty.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of training and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
No width sweep or test-error measurement around the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch generalization-gap measurement.
No sharpness or other generalization measure compared with the training–test gap.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Vanilla ResNet18 trained on CIFAR-10; compared with ResNet18 using rescaling symmetry on every parameter.

conditions.value: cosine learning rate scheduler for 200 epochs

rows.baseline: roughly 93% test accuracy for the vanilla model
rows.value: roughly 93% test accuracy for the DCS model; the DCS model higher by a small margin
rows.note: The paper reports similar final test accuracy but no training accuracy, so this result cannot establish a training–test gap.
rows.check: The approximate accuracies and conditions agree with Section B.4, but this is the study's own method compared with vanilla ResNet18 and should not be a claim-testing row. It combines two model conditions; the value belongs to DCS and the baseline to vanilla ResNet18.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
